newsitem.title: USA: S.F. gay community relieved over Cunanan death.
newsitem.headline: S.F. gay community relieved over Cunanan death.

text.p: Relief spread through San Francisco's largely gay Castro neighbourhood on Thursday at news that suspected serial killer Andrew Cunanan had committed suicide in Miami Beach.

"I think people are relieved about it, especially in this area. It just doesn't help the gay community to have a gay serial killer running around," Bob West, a 43-year-old gay man, said as he walked through the colourful Castro District, perhaps the nation's largest and best-known gay neighbourhood.
The Castro, as it is called, has been abuzz with talk of Cunanan, a 27-year-old gay gigolo suspected of killing fashion designer Gianni Versace and four other men during a cross-country murder spree.
Cunanan was found dead on Wednesday night when police stormed a Miami Beach houseboat. Police said he shot himself in the head.

Cunanan was well-known in the large gay community in San Francisco, where he had frequented gay bars and restaurants. Some reports said Cunanan met Versace backstage at the San Francisco opera in 1990.

Cunanan was last spotted in San Francisco in April and some in the gay community feared he might return. FBI "wanted" posters for Cunanan were still displayed prominently on Thursday in several shops and restaurants on Castro St.

West said he believed the case might help the FBI realise that "they need to use the gay community when there are situations like this, and not look at them as the enemy or as somebody that's not going to help them."
"People in the gay community are just as concerned about crime as anybody else," West added.
Bob Stone, a 46-year-old realtor who is gay, said: "Everybody I know is just glad that it's over and they don't have to deal with it anymore."
Stone said it was true that Cunanan's motivation would now never be known. But he added: "I don't care. It wasn't the motivation of a sane human being."

He denied that Castro residents had been afraid that Cunanan might go there. "We've been through a lot in this neighbourhood. I don't think there's too much that could make us more concerned or frightened than everything else that's gone down over the last 15 years," Stone said, referring to AIDS and economic and social changes in San Francisco.

Jim Guida, a 37-year-old gay Castro resident, said Cunanan's end was "a well-deserved death ... He did us a favour" by killing himself. Guida and several others said they thought the case had been hyped by the news media.

He also said Cunanan would have been quickly spotted if he had returned to San Francisco. "You can't hide in drag no matter how good you are," Guida said, referring to reports that Cunanan may have disguised himself as a woman.

But Randy Balch, 52, a liquor store clerk, said he was suspicious about the official report of Cunanan's death. He said it was odd that police initially reported finding no one inside the houseboat, but later said there was a body.

"I think that it could possibly be the FBI trying to make themselves look good," he said. "If that was him (Cunanan), I'm only sorry that we didn't get to find out more about what was going on in his mind," Balch said.
